text:
Priya (acme-sre): Hey team — over the last 2 days our integration with hosted inference started getting sporadic 502s with `connection reset by peer`. Happens mid-request when our token refresh cycle runs (we rotate short-lived bearer tokens every 45s). Example error from our client: `Error: read tcp 10.0.1.5:34567->34.120.1.2:443: read: connection reset by peer`. Started after we switched to session-based tokens.

Jordan (support): Sorry you're hitting that, Priya. Do you have a minimal repro (curl or SDK snippet) you can paste? Also which endpoint / model and region?

Priya (acme-sre): Using hosted inference in us-west1, endpoint /v1/generate, model: redwood-large-1. Repro (simplified):
```bash
# step 1: get short-lived token from our STS
TOKEN=eyJhbGci...short
# step 2: make long streaming request while token rotation happens
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -d '{"prompt":"long streaming prompt...","max_tokens":500}'
```
If we have our token refresher swap the token during a long request, ~30-80% of the time the request fails with the connection reset. Not always but common under our load pattern.

Jordan (support): Thanks — can repro logs and then I'll escalate. @Nikhil can you triage oncall?

Nikhil (oncall): Looking. Can you attach the full curl -v output (headers + TLs handshake) and any edge/gateway request IDs? If you have tcpdump/pcap showing the RST that helps.

Priya (acme-sre): Pasted a redacted curl -v below, includes the TLS handshake and final RESET:
```
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (34.120.1.2) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer eyJ...short
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Transfer-Encoding: chunked

< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< date: Tue, 12 Mar 2025 13:12:10 GMT
< content-type: application/json
< x-request-id: rwd_abc123
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.ai left intact
* read: Connection reset by peer
```

Nikhil (oncall): x-request-id rwd_abc123 shows gateway handled it, then connection closed by upstream. @Sofia fyi — sounds auth/token rotation related and repeatable when token changes mid-stream. Could be reuse of connection with different auth context.

Sofia (eng-runtime): Thanks @Nikhil — I'll take this. Reproduced locally with a small Go program that refreshes token during an open streaming POST. Observed the same sequence: gateway accepts connection, we reuse the host-level keepalive connection for the next request after token rotated, upstream returns 502 and TCP RST.

Sofia (eng-runtime): Root cause summary (prelim): our gateway reuses HTTP/1.1/TLS connections across requests without tying connection reuse to the Authorization token fingerprint. When the client rotates a short-lived bearer token mid-session and initiates a new request on the same TCP/TLS connection, some upstreams reject the request due to auth scope mismatch and immediately close the connection, which the client sees as `connection reset by peer`. The sequence is deterministic in our repro when the token rotation happens between the client request framing and server/auth validation.

Sofia (eng-runtime): Repro steps I used:
```bash
# 1) issue token1 (valid for 45s)
# 2) start a chunked POST using token1
# 3) after client has sent first chunks, rotate token (issue token2)
# 4) fire another request on the same http client instance (reuses connection) with token2
# 5) upstream responds 502 + TCP RST
```
Observed logs on gateway: `connection_reused_with_different_auth: true` and upstream returned 502/connection_reset.

Jordan (support): So is the actionable mitigation customer-side?

Sofia (eng-runtime): Short term workarounds:
- client: disable keepalive or set `Connection: close` for requests while rotating tokens (low perf impact if infrequent).
- client: pin token per connection (create new HTTP client after token refresh).
- server/gateway: we should avoid reusing connections across bearer token changes by checking Authorization header fingerprint when selecting a kept-alive connection.

Sofia (eng-runtime): Created ticket INF-3378 to implement token-fingerprint-aware connection pooling and added an integration test that reproduces the issue. Patch/PR: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/runtime/pull/842 (WIP). I'll aim for a canary deploy within 48h.

Priya (acme-sre): Thanks — we can do the Connection: close fallback for now. We prefer a server fix but need a short-term workaround to stop customer impact.

Jordan (support): Noted. I've given Priya the workaround steps and confirmed they can roll that change quickly. Priya — please ping if you still see failures after turning on Connection: close.

Sofia (eng-runtime): Quick debug note for the runbook: when token rotation is used, check gateway logs for `connection_reused_with_different_auth` and x-request-id; that correlates reliably.

InfraBot: New ticket created: INF-3378 by sofia (eng-runtime). Priority: P2.

Nikhil (oncall): For visibility — added INF-3378 to oncall board and added a short blameless postmortem note.

(12 hours later)

Sofia (eng-runtime): PR merged and deployed to canary; change: connection pool now keys by Authorization token fingerprint (simple HMAC of header value) for short-lived bearer tokens. Canaries look good (no increase in latency and no regression on throughput). Rolling to prod next maintenance window.

Jordan (support): @Priya when can you check if Connection: close plus our canary resolves your observed failures?

Priya (acme-sre): We enabled Connection: close yesterday afternoon and the failed rate dropped to near-zero during our load tests. We'll keep it on until you confirm prod rollout. Thanks. :thumbsup:

Sofia (eng-runtime): Prod rollout completed successfully in the maintenance window. Monitors show a drop in 502s for clients that were rotating tokens. No other regressions.

Jordan (support): Great — closing the loop. INF-3378 will stay open until we add a GA test matrix and a short doc update for clients about token best practices. Priya — feel free to reopen if you see anything else.

Priya (acme-sre): All good from our side. Thanks for the quick turnaround everyone! :tada:
